central_unknown: Rain is forecast throughout Sunday at Interlagos, creating major uncertainty around qualifying positions, race-day grip, and DNF risk — this disproportionately favors experienced wet-weather drivers like Verstappen while making rookies like Rafa Câmara and unreliable cars (Aston Martin, Cadillac) extremely risky.

budget_tiers.core: Verstappen (2x captain), Antonelli, Hamilton or Leclerc as 3rd A-tier, Red Bull or Mercedes constructor
Verstappen (2x) or Antonelli (2x), Hamilton, Mercedes constructor

budget_tiers.fills: Bortoleto + two budget B-tiers from Hulkenberg/Bearman/Sainz/Lindblad

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: Consensus #1 captain across all channels. Won both wet races this season (Singapore & Malaysia). Finished P3 in both FP1 and FP2. Exceptional Interlagos record — won 3 of last 4 races here. Wet weather is his superpower. ML projects 25.9 exp pts, ppm 1.62, MEDIUM risk for Las Vegas (nearest available ML data); channels unanimously rate him as the top pick for São Paulo, especially in changeable conditions. ZachGP explicitly names him as 2x pick.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lando Norris
captains.reason: Only 4.2% ownership in Global Top 500. McLaren brought their biggest upgrade package of the season to Interlagos. P1 in FP1, P2 in FP2. Won this race last season. Strong in wet conditions historically. FanAmp notes betting lines show him closing the gap to top two. ML projects 20.3 exp pts at Las Vegas — but channels flag his FP pace and upgrades may push him higher here. ZachGP considers him a differential but isn't personally going near McLaren; FanAmp and PolePosition are more bullish.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Home GP, P8 in both FP1 and FP2. Strong pace from Audi. Budget-increasing asset — needs only -12 for min price rise, -7 for max. Consensus best cheap B-tier across all channels. Potential DOTD if he performs well at home.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Trusted wet-weather veteran per FanAmp. Has been adding value consistently. CAUTION: Freddy Slater had reliability issues in Hulk's car during FP1, and Hulk did not set a time in FP2. Monitor FP3 closely — if he completes laps, he's a strong hold. Possible engine penalty would actually make him a better fantasy asset (back of grid overtake points).

buy.name: Oliver Bearman
buy.note: Scored 30 pts at São Paulo last season and 14 pts in 2024 when he subbed in. P12 FP1, P10 FP2. Loves this track. PolePosition highlights his strong Interlagos history across multiple years.

consider.name: Carlos Sainz
consider.note: FanAmp warming up to Williams duo in mixed conditions. Needs only 2 pts for min price rise. Experienced wet-weather driver. FP1/FP2 pace not highlighted but Williams improving lately.

consider.name: Alex Albon
consider.note: FanAmp also warming to Albon for wet conditions. Williams had some FP1 issues but are a viable mid-budget option.

consider.name: Franco Colapinto
consider.note: Differential at 2.2% ownership in top 500. P9 FP1, P11 FP2. Alpine showed decent pace. But terrible Interlagos history (-10 in 2024, -16 in 2025). PolePosition considers him only as a Hulkenberg backup.

consider.name: Arvid Lindblad
consider.note: Budget option from Racing Bulls. ZachGP includes him in team builds. Decent budget-preserving filler.

avoid: Rafa Câmara — debut race, never raced at Interlagos, first time in 2026 car during FP1, wet conditions are worst-case for a rookie. Betting lines show him among the most likely first retirements. Consensus avoid across all channels.
Lance Stroll — finished only 2 of last 9 races. DNF magnet. Budget floor but not worth the -25 risk.
Fernando Alonso — serial DNFs in the Aston Martin. Another DNF-after-DNF driver per ZachGP.
Valtteri Bottas — budget floor but same DNF problems as other Cadillac/Aston Martin assets.
Sergio Perez — less FP running time, unreliable, limited upside.
Esteban Ocon — INACTIVE DRIVER. Must remove immediately or face -25 per race.
Rio Hirakawa — INACTIVE DRIVER. Must remove immediately or face -25 per race.
Pierre Gasly — ZachGP places him on the do-not-use list; Alpine pace not strong enough relative to budget.
Oscar Piastri — still looks lost in the McLaren, gave up FP1 seat. Only Norris worth considering from McLaren.
George Russell — 5-place grid penalty, recent form of P9/P8/P6 since Baku win, Mercedes weak in dirty air. Upside capped around 20-25 pts per FanAmp. Better options available.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: If you're stuck with multiple dead assets (Ocon, Hirakawa, Stroll, Bottas) and need a full restructure to get Verstappen + Antonelli + quality B-tiers, this is a reasonable week to wildcard. Rain creates variance that could reward a well-constructed team. However, Las Vegas is also a strong wildcard candidate if you can manage with transfers this week.

chips.name: Autopilot (2x Captain)
chips.reason: ZachGP explicitly recommends using the 2x on Verstappen this weekend. Wet conditions at Interlagos historically produce dominant Verstappen performances. His ceiling is enormous if rain materializes. If you've already used autopilot, manually captaining Verstappen is the consensus play.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: No channel recommends Limitless for São Paulo. Save for a weekend with clearer pace hierarchies and less weather variance — Las Vegas or end-of-season races are better candidates.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Hold Final Fix for a weekend where a late qualifying surprise (engine penalty, crash) creates a clear last-minute optimization. Could be useful if Hulkenberg situation clarifies late.

watch_items: Hulkenberg's car reliability: Freddy Slater's FP1 red flag and Hulk's zero laps in FP2 are major red flags. If Hulk doesn't complete meaningful FP3 running, consider swapping to Colapinto, Sainz, or Bearman.

Verstappen engine penalty: He has hinted at a potential late-season engine penalty. Small chance it comes at Brazil. If announced, he becomes an EVEN BETTER asset due to overtake points — do not panic sell.

Rain timing on Sunday: Greatest chance of rain in early afternoon per weather analyst Ralpho. Even if F1 adjusts start time, rain is predicted throughout the day. This favors veterans and punishes rookies/unreliable machinery.

McLaren upgrades: Biggest upgrade package on the grid. Chris Medlin reports these may be 2027 components being tested. Monitor FP3/quali to see if Norris pace from FP1/FP2 holds — could validate him as a serious differential.
Câmara's debut: Emotional home race story but extremely risky fantasy asset. Do not chase the narrative unless FP3 shows shocking pace.

Mercedes constructor vs Red Bull constructor: Russell's 5-place penalty gives him overtake upside that could swing the Russell vs Hadjar matchup in Mercedes' favor. FanAmp prefers Mercedes constructor over Red Bull this week despite giving up 0.3M price gain potential.
arc: São Paulo is a high-variance race due to weather uncertainty, making it a weekend where getting the captain right (Verstappen in rain, Antonelli in dry) is worth more than optimizing B-tier selections. The Hulkenberg reliability situation could cascade into future weeks if Audi takes engine penalties. McLaren's upgrade package is potentially the biggest development story — if it translates to genuine pace, Norris becomes a factor for Las Vegas and beyond. With Antonelli having already clinched the WDC and Mercedes potentially holding back their engine upgrade, the constructor battle shifts focus to value extraction. Las Vegas (Round 23) is a power circuit where Mercedes and Red Bull should dominate, making it a strong Limitless or 3x candidate — plan your chip sequencing accordingly. Budget management is critical in these final rounds: prioritize assets that score points over those that gain price, as channels unanimously agree end-of-season rank matters more than budget.
